payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Transform the image into a pencil drawing.
node.criteria: Return yes only when support 1 passes: the edited image is rendered as a pencil drawing representing its visual content. Return no when support 1 fails and support 2 fails, establishing that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when support 1 fails and support 2 passes, establishing progress without complete fulfillment. Return unknown when the available observations do not establish one of those outcomes, including when a needed observation is unknown. Support 2 is skipped when support 1 passes; on that path, the endpoint evidence alone establishes completion, so the skipped progress check is unobserved and earns no independent credit. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.. Reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation..

node_traces.evidence: Support 1 passes: the edited image preserves the visual content and renders it with pencil-like shading and sketch texture. This establishes completion; support 2 was conditionally skipped and is not needed.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image preserves the meal and surrounding objects, rendered in muted grayscale with visible pencil-like shading and sketch texture.

This is visual evidence for partial fulfillment, not a transport or schema failure. The node’s binding is broadly appropriate; repair its decision criterion so a positive endpoint requires the requested style to be convincingly achieved across the image, rather than treating any pencil-like shading or texture as sufficient. Preserve the separate progress check and the rule that unrelated edits do not count. Also avoid treating a conditionally skipped support as evidence: the current trace explicitly skips s2 after s1 passes, so it cannot establish partial progress or independently validate completion. Ensure the endpoint logic can distinguish incomplete-but-relevant style progress from full completion, and returns unknown when the necessary visual observations are unavailable. The high-confidence pass despite visible residual color suggests the criterion is too permissive, not that confidence or repeated variation alone proves the edit absent."}
